academic_standards_framework.AS2: Reading the text (given), understanding and interpretation
academic_standards_framework.AS4: Reflection on contemporary issues and questioning

core_themes: French society during late eighteenth century: The Three Estates, feudal privileges, tax burden on Third Estate.
The Outbreak of the Revolution: Estates General meeting May 5, 1789; National Assembly; Storming of Bastille July 14, 1789.
France becomes a Constitutional Monarchy: Declaration of Rights of Man and Citizen.
France abolishes Monarchy and becomes a Republic: The Convention, Reign of Terror under Robespierre (Jacobins), Guillotine.
The Directory and the Rise of Napoleon Bonaparte; Abolition of slavery in French colonies.
learning_outcomes: Understand the socio-economic causes of the French Revolution.
Examine the Declaration of Rights of Man and Citizen as a landmark in human rights.
Analyze the legacy of French revolutionary ideas of liberty, equality, and fraternity across Europe.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Describe the circumstances leading to the outbreak of revolutionary protest in France.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఫ్రాన్స్‌లో విప్లవాత్మక నిరసనలు చెలరేగడానికి దారితీసిన పరిస్థితులను వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Read the Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen. Which fundamental rights are emphasized as natural and inalienable?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: మానవ హక్కుల ప్రకటనను చదివి, సహజమైన మరియు పరాయీకరించలేనివిగా పేర్కొన్న ప్రాథమిక హక్కులు ఏవో రాయండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of France, locate and label the following revolutionary centres: Paris, Nantes, Bordeaux, and Marseilles.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఫ్రాన్స్ అవుట్‌లైన్ మ్యాప్‌లో ప్యారిస్, నాంటెస్, బోర్డియక్స్ మరియు మార్సెల్లెస్ నగరాలను గుర్తించి పేర్లు రాయండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain the significance of the revolutionary slogan 'Liberty, Equality, Fraternity' in modern democracies.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఆధునిక ప్రజాస్వామ్యాలలో 'స్వేచ్ఛ, సమానత్వం, సౌభ్రాతృత్వం' అనే విప్లవ నినాదం ప్రాముఖ్యతను వివరించండి.

history.title_en: Socialism in Europe and the Russian Revolution
core_themes: The Age of Social Change: Liberals, Radicals, and Conservatives.
Industrial Society and the Coming of Socialism to Europe: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels.
The Russian Empire in 1914: Economy and Society, 1905 Revolution, Bloody Sunday, Duma.
The First World War and the Russian Empire: February Revolution in Petrograd, fall of Tsarist autocracy.
The October Revolution of 1917: Lenin and the Bolsheviks, Soviet power.
Civil War, Making a Socialist Society, and Stalin's Collectivization program.
learning_outcomes: Trace the development of socialist ideology in 19th-century Europe.
Examine the causes and course of the February and October Revolutions in Russia.
Analyze the global impact of the Russian Revolution and the USSR.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What were the main differences between Liberals, Radicals, and Conservatives in 19th-century Europe?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: 19వ శతాబ్దపు ఐరోపాలో ఉదారవాదులు, తీవ్రవాదులు మరియు సాంప్రదాయవాదుల మధ్య గల ప్రధాన భేదాలు ఏమిటి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain the major events leading to the October Revolution of 1917 in Russia and the role played by Vladimir Lenin.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: రష్యాలో 1917 అక్టోబర్ విప్లవానికి దారితీసిన ప్రధాన సంఘటనలను మరియు వ్లాదిమిర్ లెనిన్ పోషించిన పాత్రను వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What were the effects of the collectivization program introduced by Stalin on Russian peasants?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: రష్యన్ రైతులపై స్టాలిన్ ప్రవేశపెట్టిన సమిష్టి వ్యవసాయ విధానం (కలెక్టివైజేషన్) చూపిన ప్రభావాలు ఏమిటి?

history.title_en: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
core_themes: Birth of the Weimar Republic after World War I; Treaty of Versailles; Economic Crisis (1923) and Great Depression.
Hitler's Rise to Power: Nazi propaganda, speechcraft, Enabling Act of 1933, establishment of totalitarian dictatorship.
The Nazi Worldview: Racial hierarchy, Nordic Aryans, Anti-Semitism, Lebensraum (living space).
Youth in Nazi Germany: Jungvolk, Hitler Youth; Motherhood cult.
The Holocaust: Ghettos, gas chambers, Nuremberg trials.
learning_outcomes: Understand the humiliating impact of the Treaty of Versailles on Germany.
Explain the political and economic conditions that enabled Hitler's fascist dictatorship.
Sensitize students against racism, discrimination, and genocide.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain why the Weimar Republic was politically fragile in Germany.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: జర్మనీలో వీమర్ రిపబ్లిక్ రాజకీయంగా ఎందుకు బలహీనంగా ఉండిందో వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What was the Holocaust? Why is it considered one of the darkest chapters in human history?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: హోలోకాస్ట్ (మారణహోమం) అంటే ఏమిటి? మానవ చరిత్రలో ఇది అత్యంత చీకటి అధ్యాయంగా ఎందుకు పరిగణించబడుతుంది?

core_themes: Deforestation under British Rule: Timber for Royal Navy, railway sleepers, commercial crops (tea, coffee, rubber).
Scientific Forestry: Dietrich Brandis, Indian Forest Act of 1865 and 1878 amendments (Reserved, Protected, Village forests).
Impact on forest dwellers: Shifting cultivation banned, hunting criminalized, forced labour.
Rebellion in the Forest: Bastar rebellion (1910) led by Gunda Dhur; Dutch forest laws in Java (Blandongdiensten system) and Saminist movement.
learning_outcomes: Understand the commercial and imperial reasons for British deforestation in India.
Examine the loss of tribal livelihoods and autonomy under colonial forest laws.
Compare forest resistance in Bastar (India) with Java (Indonesia).

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain why the British introduced 'Scientific Forestry' in India. What were its consequences for forest communities?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: బ్రిటిష్ వారు భారతదేశంలో 'శాస్త్రీయ అటవీ విధానాన్ని' ఎందుకు ప్రవేశపెట్టారు? అటవీ సమాజాలపై దాని పరిణామాలు ఏమిటి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: How did the 1910 Bastar Rebellion reflect the grievances of indigenous tribal communities?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: 1910 బస్తర్ తిరుగుబాటు స్థానిక ఆదివాసీ తెగల సమస్యలను ఎలా ప్రతిబింబించింది?

core_themes: Pastoral Nomads in India: Gujjar Bakarwals (Jammu & Kashmir), Gaddis (Himachal Pradesh), Dhangars (Maharashtra), Raikas (Rajasthan).
Colonial Rule and Pastoral Life: Waste Land Rules, Forest Acts, Criminal Tribes Act of 1871, Grazing tax.
Pastoralism in Africa: Maasai community of East Africa, loss of grazing lands, creation of game reserves (Serengeti, Maasai Mara).
learning_outcomes: Understand pastoral nomadic life as an ecologically sustainable adaptation to arid and mountain environments.
Examine how colonial borders, grazing taxes, and wildlife reserves destroyed traditional pastoral economies.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain how the seasonal movement of the Gujjar Bakarwals is adapted to the mountain environment.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: గుజ్జర్ బకర్వాల్స్ పశువుల కాపరుల కాలానుగుణ వలసలు పర్వత పర్యావరణానికి ఎలా అనుగుణంగా ఉంటాయో వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why did the colonial state consider pastoralists as unproductive and view mobile communities with suspicion?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: వలస పాలకులు పశుపోషకులను నిరుపయోగమైన వారిగా ఎందుకు భావించారు మరియు సంచార జాతులను అనుమానంతో ఎందుకు చూశారు?

core_themes: Location: Entirely in Northern Hemisphere; Latitudes 8°4'N to 37°6'N, Longitudes 68°7'E to 97°25'E.
Tropic of Cancer (23°30'N) divides India into almost two equal halves.
Size: Total area 3.28 million sq km (2.4% of total world area); 7th largest country; Land boundary 15,200 km; Coastline 7,516.6 km.
Standard Meridian of India (82°30'E passing through Mirzapur in UP); IST is GMT + 5:30.
India and the World: Strategic central location at head of Indian Ocean; Neighbours (Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Maldives).
learning_outcomes: Locate India's latitudinal and longitudinal extent on the world globe.
Understand why 82°30'E longitude was selected as the Standard Meridian of India.
Identify India's strategic maritime and land neighbours.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: The sun rises two hours earlier in Arunachal Pradesh as compared to Gujarat in the west, but the watches show the same time. How does this happen?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: గుజరాత్‌తో పోలిస్తే అరుణాచల్ ప్రదేశ్‌లో సూర్యుడు రెండు గంటల ముందే ఉదయిస్తాడు, కానీ గడియారాలు ఒకే సమయాన్ని చూపుతాయి. ఇది ఎలా సాధ్యం?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, identify and locate: (a) Tropic of Cancer, (b) Standard Meridian of India, (c) Southernmost tip of Indian mainland.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ అవుట్‌లైన్ మ్యాప్‌లో గుర్తించండి: (a) కర్కట రేఖ, (b) ప్రామాణిక రేఖాంశం (82°30' తూర్పు), (c) భారతదేశ ప్రధాన భూభాగ దక్షిణ అగ్రం (కన్యాకుమారి).

core_themes: Theory of Plate Tectonics: Convergent, Divergent, Transform boundaries; Gondwanaland breakup.
The Himalayan Mountains: Himadri (Greater Himalayas), Himachal (Lesser Himalayas), Shiwaliks (Outer Himalayas).
The Northern Plains: Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar, Khadar; Alluvial deposits of Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra.
The Peninsular Plateau: Central Highlands, Deccan Plateau, Western Ghats (Anamudi 2695 m), Eastern Ghats (Mahendragiri 1501 m).
The Indian Desert (Thar), The Coastal Plains (Konkan, Kannad, Malabar, Coromandel, Northern Circars), and The Islands (Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar).
learning_outcomes: Understand tectonic plate movements creating Himalayas and Indo-Gangetic plains.
Compare the physical features of Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats.
Classify Northern Plains based on relief features.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Distinguish between Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: పశ్చిమ కనుమలు మరియు తూర్పు కనుమల మధ్య గల భేదాలను రాయండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Contrast the relief of the Himalayan region with that of the Peninsular plateau.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: హిమాలయ ప్రాంత భౌగోళిక స్వరూపాలను ద్వీపకల్ప పీఠభూమి స్వరూపాలతో పోల్చి భేదాలను రాయండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, locate and label: Kanchenjunga peak, Chota Nagpur plateau, and Malabar Coast.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ అవుట్‌లైన్ మ్యాప్‌లో కాంచన్‌జంగా శిఖరం, చోటానాగ్‌పూర్ పీఠభూమి, మలబార్ తీరాలను గుర్తించండి.

core_themes: Drainage basins, water divides, and drainage patterns (Dendritic, Trellis, Rectangular, Radial).
Himalayan Rivers: The Indus River System, The Ganga River System, The Brahmaputra River System (perennial, antecedent).
Peninsular Rivers: Narmada and Tapi (rift valleys, flowing into Arabian Sea), Godavari (Dakshin Ganga), Mahanadi, Krishna, Kaveri (flowing into Bay of Bengal).
Lakes of India: Fresh water lakes (Wular, Dal, Nainital, Loktak) and Salt water lakes (Sambhar, Chilika, Pulicat).
Role of rivers in the economy and National River Conservation Plan (NRCP).
learning_outcomes: Distinguish between Himalayan and Peninsular river systems.
Explain the economic importance of freshwater lakes and rivers in agriculture and power generation.
Identify causes of river pollution and measures for river cleaning.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Compare the east-flowing and west-flowing rivers of the Peninsular plateau.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ద్వీపకల్ప పీఠభూమిలోని తూర్పుగా ప్రవహించే నదులు మరియు పశ్చిమంగా ప్రవహించే నదులను పోల్చండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, trace the course of the River Godavari and River Narmada, and mark Chilika Lake.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ పటంలో గోదావరి, నర్మదా నదుల ప్రవాహ మార్గాలను మరియు చిల్కా సరస్సును గుర్తించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why are rivers considered the lifelines of human civilization? Mention two steps to prevent river pollution.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: నదులను మానవ నాగరికతకు జీవనాధారాలుగా ఎందుకు పరిగణిస్తారు? నదీ కాలుష్యాన్ని నివారించే రెండు మార్గాలను తెలపండి.

core_themes: Difference between weather and climate.
Climatic controls: Latitude, Altitude, Pressure and wind systems, Distance from the sea (Continentality), Ocean currents, Relief.
Mechanism of the Indian Monsoon: ITCZ (Inter Tropical Convergence Zone), El Nino, Southern Oscillation (ENSO), Jet Streams.
Seasons of India: Cold weather season (Winter), Hot weather season (Summer), Advancing Monsoon (South-West Monsoon), Retreating Monsoon (North-East Monsoon / Cyclones).
Distribution of rainfall and Monsoon as a unifying bond.
learning_outcomes: Explain the factors influencing the climate of India.
Describe the mechanism of onset and withdrawal of the monsoon.
Analyze the distribution of rainfall across western coast vs interior Deccan.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What are the six major climatic controls of any place?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఏదైనా ప్రాంతం యొక్క శీతోష్ణస్థితిని నియంత్రించే ఆరు ప్రధాన కారకాలు ఏవి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why does the Coromandel Coast receive winter rainfall?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: కోరమాండల్ తీరానికి శీతాకాలంలో వర్షపాతం ఎందుకు లభిస్తుంది?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, locate Mawsynram (highest rainfall in the world) and regions receiving less than 20 cm rainfall.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ పటంలో ప్రపంచంలోనే అత్యధిక వర్షపాతం నమోదయ్యే మాసిన్‌రామ్ మరియు 20 సెం.మీ. కంటే తక్కువ వర్షపాతం పొందే ప్రాంతాలను గుర్తించండి.

core_themes: Factors affecting diversity of flora and fauna: Relief (Land, Soil) and Climate (Temperature, Photoperiod, Precipitation).
Types of Vegetation: Tropical Evergreen Forests, Tropical Deciduous Forests (Monsoon forests), Tropical Thorn Forests and Scrubs, Montane Forests, Mangrove Forests (Sundarbans).
Wildlife diversity in India; Endemic and endangered species.
Conservation of Forests and Wildlife: National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves (18 in India, e.g. Nilgiri, Sunderbans).
learning_outcomes: Identify ecological conditions required for various natural vegetation types in India.
Understand the importance of Sundarbans mangroves and biodiversity conservation.
Appreciate wildlife protection laws (Wildlife Protection Act 1972).

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Distinguish between Tropical Evergreen Forests and Tropical Deciduous Forests.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఉష్ణమండల సతతహరిత అరణ్యాలు మరియు ఉష్ణమండల ఆకురాల్చే అడవుల మధ్య గల భేదాలను వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, mark Kaziranga National Park, Gir Forest, and Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ పటంలో కాజిరంగా జాతీయ ఉద్యానవనం, గిర్ అభయారణ్యం, మరియు సుందర్‌బన్స్ బయోస్పియర్ రిజర్వ్‌లను గుర్తించండి.

core_themes: Population Size and Distribution: Census of India, population density (people per sq km).
Population Growth and Processes of Population Change: Birth rate, Death rate, Migration (Internal and International).
Age Composition: Children (below 15), Working age (15-59), Aged (60+); Dependency ratio.
Sex Ratio: Number of females per 1000 males; Literacy rate.
Occupational Structure: Primary, Secondary, Tertiary sectors; National Population Policy (NPP 2000).
learning_outcomes: Explain the components of population change: fertility, mortality, and migration.
Interpret population pyramids and age sex composition.
Understand key objectives of National Population Policy 2000.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What are the three main components of population change? Explain how each influences population growth.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: జనాభా మార్పుకు గల మూడు ప్రధాన కారకాలు ఏవి? ప్రతి ఒక్కటి జనాభా పెరుగుదలను ఎలా ప్రభావితం చేస్తుందో వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What is meant by Sex Ratio? Why is a favorable sex ratio considered an indicator of women empowerment?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: స్త్రీ-పురుష నిష్పత్తి (సెక్స్ రేషియో) అనగా ఏమిటి? అనుకూలమైన స్త్రీ-పురుష నిష్పత్తి మహిళా సాధికారతకు సూచికగా ఎందుకు పరిగణించబడుతుంది?

core_themes: Simple Definition: Democracy is a form of government in which rulers are elected by the people.

Features of Democracy: Major decisions by elected leaders (Pakistan under Musharraf case); Free and fair electoral competition (China and Mexico cases); One person, one vote, one value (Fiji, Saudi Arabia, Estonia cases); Rule of law and respect for rights (Zimbabwe under Mugabe case).
Arguments against Democracy: Instability, delays, political competition, corruption.
Arguments for Democracy: Accountable government, improves decision quality, accommodates diversity, enhances dignity of citizens.
learning_outcomes: Distinguish between genuine democracy and facade democratic systems.
Critically evaluate arguments for and against democracy.
Appreciate the democratic principles of equality, accountability, and rule of law.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain the four core features of a democratic government.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ప్రజాస్వామ్య ప్రభుత్వానికి గల నాలుగు ముఖ్యమైన లక్షణాలను వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: 'Democracy is better than any other form of government in responding to the needs of the people.' Justify this statement with examples.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: 'ప్రజల అవసరాలకు స్పందించడంలో ప్రజాస్వామ్యం ఇతర ప్రభుత్వ రూపాల కంటే మెరుగైనది.' ఉదాహరణలతో ఈ ప్రకటనను సమర్థించండి.

core_themes: Democratic Constitution in South Africa: Apartheid struggle, Nelson Mandela, transition to non-racial democracy in 1994.
Why do we need a Constitution? Establishes trust, specifies decision-making authority, limits government power, expresses aspirations.
Making of the Indian Constitution: Constituent Assembly, Motilal Nehru draft (1928), Karachi session (1931), Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
Guiding Values of the Indian Constitution: Preamble: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic, Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity.
learning_outcomes: Understand the struggle against apartheid and the making of South African constitution.
Analyze the historical consensus and debates within India's Constituent Assembly.
Examine the core constitutional values enshrined in the Preamble.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What were the challenges faced by the makers of the Indian Constitution during its drafting?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారత రాజ్యాంగ రూపకల్పన సమయంలో రాజ్యాంగ నిర్మాతలు ఎదుర్కొన్న ప్రధాన సవాళ్లు ఏమిటి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Read the Preamble to the Constitution of India. Explain the significance of the terms 'Secular' and 'Republic'.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారత రాజ్యాంగ ప్రవేశికను చదివి, అందులోని 'లౌకిక' మరియు 'గణతంత్ర' పదాల అంతరార్థాన్ని వివరించండి.

core_themes: Why Elections? Mechanism for citizens to choose representatives and policy makers.
What makes an election democratic? Universal adult suffrage, genuine choices, regular intervals, free and fair process.
Electoral system in India: Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha constituencies, Reserved constituencies for SC and ST.
Voters' list (Electoral Roll), Nomination of candidates, Election campaign, Model Code of Conduct, Polling and counting.
Independent Election Commission of India (ECI): Powers, autonomous constitutional status, acceptance of election outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Understand how periodic elections ensure representative democratic accountability.
Evaluate the powers and constitutional independence of the Election Commission of India.
Explain provisions ensuring free, fair, and inclusive elections.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What powers make the Election Commission of India independent and powerful?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారత ఎన్నికల సంఘానికి గల ఏ అధికారాలు దానిని స్వతంత్రమైన మరియు శక్తివంతమైన సంస్థగా నిలబెడుతున్నాయి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What is the Model Code of Conduct for election campaigns? Mention any three prohibitions under it.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఎన్నికల ప్రవర్తనా నియమావళి (మోడల్ కోడ్ ఆఫ్ కండక్ట్) అంటే ఏమిటి? దాని కింద విధించిన ఏవైనా మూడు నిబంధనలను పేర్కొనండి.

core_themes: How a Major Policy Decision is Taken: Office Memorandum example, Mandal Commission report.
Parliament: Need for political institutions, two Houses (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha), powers comparison.
Political Executive: Difference between Political Executive (Ministers) and Permanent Executive (Civil Servants).
Prime Minister and Council of Ministers: Cabinet, powers of Prime Minister; President of India (Head of State).
Judiciary: Supreme Court of India, High Courts, Judicial Review, Public Interest Litigation (PIL), Independence of Judiciary.
learning_outcomes: Analyze the division of powers between Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary.
Compare the legislative and financial powers of Lok Sabha versus Rajya Sabha.
Understand the independence of judiciary and judicial review.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why does the Lok Sabha exercise supreme power over the Rajya Sabha in matters of money bills?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ధన బిల్లుల విషయంలో రాజ్యసభ కంటే లోక్‌సభకు అత్యున్నత అధికారాలు ఎందుకు ఉన్నాయి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Distinguish between the Political Executive and the Permanent Executive.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: రాజకీయ కార్యనిర్వాహక వర్గం మరియు శాశ్వత కార్యనిర్వాహక వర్గం (సివిల్ సర్వీసెస్) మధ్య గల భేదాలను వివరించండి.

core_themes: Life without rights: Prison in Guantanamo Bay (US), Citizens' rights in Saudi Arabia, Ethnic massacre in Kosovo.
Rights in a Democracy: Definition of rights as reasonable claims of persons recognized by society and sanctioned by law.

Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32).
Expanding scope of rights: RTI, Right to Education, Human Rights Commission.
learning_outcomes: Appreciate the vital role of constitutional fundamental rights in protecting individual liberty.
Examine Article 32 as the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution' (Ambedkar).
Understand the evolving landscape of socioeconomic human rights.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why is the Right to Constitutional Remedies considered the heart and soul of our Constitution?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: రాజ్యాంగ పరిహార హక్కును మన రాజ్యాంగానికి గుండెకాయ మరియు ఆత్మగా ఎందుకు భావిస్తారు?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain how the Right to Equality protects citizens against discrimination in India.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశంలో పౌరులను వివక్ష నుండి సమానత్వపు హక్కు ఏ విధంగా కాపాడుతుందో వివరించండి.

core_themes: Overview of production: Organization of production (Land, Labour, Physical Capital, Human Capital).
Farming in Palampur: Land is fixed; Multiple cropping, Green Revolution with HYV seeds, chemical fertilizers, irrigation tube-wells.
Impact of Green Revolution on soil fertility and groundwater depletion.
Land distribution among farmers: Small vs medium and large farmers.
Non-farm activities in Palampur: Dairy farming, small-scale manufacturing, shopkeeping, transport services.
learning_outcomes: Understand the four essential factors of production: Land, Labour, Capital, and Enterprise.
Examine the benefits and ecological drawbacks of Green Revolution agricultural modernization.
Identify non-farm rural livelihood opportunities.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain the four requirements for the production of goods and services.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: వస్తువులు మరియు సేవల ఉత్పత్తికి అవసరమైన నాలుగు ప్రధాన కారకాలను వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What are the environmental hazards associated with excessive use of chemical fertilizers in Green Revolution farming?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: హరిత విప్లవ వ్యవసాయంలో రసాయన ఎరువుల మితిమీరిన వినియోగం వల్ల కలిగే పర్యావరణ ముప్పులు ఏమిటి?

core_themes: Overview: Human capital formation through investment in education, training, and healthcare.
Economic Activities by Men and Women: Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary sectors; Market and non-market activities.
Quality of Population: Education (literacy rates, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan), Health (life expectancy, infant mortality rate).
Unemployment: Disguised unemployment, Seasonal unemployment in rural areas, Educated unemployment in urban areas.
Consequences of unemployment: Wastage of manpower, economic overload, social unrest.
learning_outcomes: Understand how human capital increases productivity and national income.
Differentiate between seasonal and disguised unemployment.
Examine public investment in education and public healthcare systems.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What is the difference between economic activities and non-economic activities?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఆర్థిక కార్యకలాపాలు మరియు ఆర్థికేతర కార్యకలాపాల మధ్య గల వ్యత్యాసం ఏమిటి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What is disguised unemployment? Give an agricultural example.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ప్రచ్ఛన్న నిరుద్యోగం అనగా ఏమిటి? వ్యవసాయ రంగం నుండి ఒక ఉదాహరణ ఇవ్వండి.

core_themes: Dimensions of poverty: Hunger, lack of shelter, safe drinking water, healthcare, sanitation, job insecurity.
Poverty as seen by social scientists: Social exclusion, vulnerability.
Poverty Line concept: Minimum subsistence level, calorie norms (2400 rural, 2100 urban), monetary value.
Poverty estimates in India; Vulnerable groups (SC, ST, landless agricultural labourers).
Inter-state disparities in poverty (high in Bihar, Odisha; low in Kerala, Punjab).
Anti-Poverty Measures: Promotion of economic growth; Targeted anti-poverty programmes: MGNREGA 2005, PMRY, PMGY, AAY.
learning_outcomes: Understand the multidimensional nature of poverty and poverty line estimation.
Analyze inter-state and social group disparities in poverty incidence.
Evaluate government welfare and employment generation schemes (MGNREGA).

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: How is the poverty line estimated in India? Explain the calorie and monetary criteria.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశంలో పేదరిక రేఖను ఎలా అంచనా వేస్తారు? కేలరీల వినియోగం మరియు ఆదాయ ప్రమాణాలను వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Discuss the major features of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) 2005.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: మహాత్మా గాంధీ జాతీయ గ్రామీణ ఉపాధి హామీ చట్టం (MGNREGA) 2005 యొక్క ముఖ్య లక్షణాలను చర్చించండి.

core_themes: What is Food Security? Availability, Accessibility, and Affordability of food to all citizens.
Why Food Security? Famine of Bengal (1943), disaster mitigation, food insecurity during natural calamities.
Who are Food-Insecure? Landless agricultural labourers, traditional artisans, urban casual workers, vulnerable castes.
Food Security System in India: Buffer Stock (FCI procurement at Minimum Support Price - MSP) and Public Distribution System (PDS - Fair Price Shops).
Role of Cooperatives in Food Security: Amul (Gujarat), Mother Dairy (Delhi), Academy of Development Science (Grain banks in Maharashtra).
learning_outcomes: Understand the triple pillars of food security: Availability, Accessibility, Affordability.
Explain the functioning of Buffer Stock and the Public Distribution System (PDS).
Appreciate the vital role of agricultural and consumer cooperatives in ensuring food security.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What is Buffer Stock? Why is it created by the government?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: బఫర్ స్టాక్ (నిల్వ ఆహార ధాన్యాలు) అనగా ఏమిటి? ప్రభుత్వం దీనిని ఎందుకు నిర్వహిస్తుంది?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain the role of the Public Distribution System (PDS) in ensuring food security in India.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశంలో ఆహార భద్రతను కల్పించడంలో ప్రజా పంపిణీ వ్యవస్థ (PDS) పోషిస్తున్న పాత్రను వివరించండి.

core_themes: French society during late eighteenth century: The Three Estates, feudal privileges, tax burden on Third Estate.
The Outbreak of the Revolution: Estates General meeting May 5, 1789; National Assembly; Storming of Bastille July 14, 1789.
France becomes a Constitutional Monarchy: Declaration of Rights of Man and Citizen.
France abolishes Monarchy and becomes a Republic: The Convention, Reign of Terror under Robespierre (Jacobins), Guillotine.
The Directory and the Rise of Napoleon Bonaparte; Abolition of slavery in French colonies.
learning_outcomes: Understand the socio-economic causes of the French Revolution.
Examine the Declaration of Rights of Man and Citizen as a landmark in human rights.
Analyze the legacy of French revolutionary ideas of liberty, equality, and fraternity across Europe.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Describe the circumstances leading to the outbreak of revolutionary protest in France.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఫ్రాన్స్‌లో విప్లవాత్మక నిరసనలు చెలరేగడానికి దారితీసిన పరిస్థితులను వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Read the Declaration of the Rights of Man and Citizen. Which fundamental rights are emphasized as natural and inalienable?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: మానవ హక్కుల ప్రకటనను చదివి, సహజమైన మరియు పరాయీకరించలేనివిగా పేర్కొన్న ప్రాథమిక హక్కులు ఏవో రాయండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of France, locate and label the following revolutionary centres: Paris, Nantes, Bordeaux, and Marseilles.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఫ్రాన్స్ అవుట్‌లైన్ మ్యాప్‌లో ప్యారిస్, నాంటెస్, బోర్డియక్స్ మరియు మార్సెల్లెస్ నగరాలను గుర్తించి పేర్లు రాయండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain the significance of the revolutionary slogan 'Liberty, Equality, Fraternity' in modern democracies.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఆధునిక ప్రజాస్వామ్యాలలో 'స్వేచ్ఛ, సమానత్వం, సౌభ్రాతృత్వం' అనే విప్లవ నినాదం ప్రాముఖ్యతను వివరించండి.

chapters.title_en: Socialism in Europe and the Russian Revolution
core_themes: The Age of Social Change: Liberals, Radicals, and Conservatives.
Industrial Society and the Coming of Socialism to Europe: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels.
The Russian Empire in 1914: Economy and Society, 1905 Revolution, Bloody Sunday, Duma.
The First World War and the Russian Empire: February Revolution in Petrograd, fall of Tsarist autocracy.
The October Revolution of 1917: Lenin and the Bolsheviks, Soviet power.
Civil War, Making a Socialist Society, and Stalin's Collectivization program.
learning_outcomes: Trace the development of socialist ideology in 19th-century Europe.
Examine the causes and course of the February and October Revolutions in Russia.
Analyze the global impact of the Russian Revolution and the USSR.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What were the main differences between Liberals, Radicals, and Conservatives in 19th-century Europe?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: 19వ శతాబ్దపు ఐరోపాలో ఉదారవాదులు, తీవ్రవాదులు మరియు సాంప్రదాయవాదుల మధ్య గల ప్రధాన భేదాలు ఏమిటి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain the major events leading to the October Revolution of 1917 in Russia and the role played by Vladimir Lenin.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: రష్యాలో 1917 అక్టోబర్ విప్లవానికి దారితీసిన ప్రధాన సంఘటనలను మరియు వ్లాదిమిర్ లెనిన్ పోషించిన పాత్రను వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What were the effects of the collectivization program introduced by Stalin on Russian peasants?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: రష్యన్ రైతులపై స్టాలిన్ ప్రవేశపెట్టిన సమిష్టి వ్యవసాయ విధానం (కలెక్టివైజేషన్) చూపిన ప్రభావాలు ఏమిటి?

chapters.title_en: Nazism and the Rise of Hitler
core_themes: Birth of the Weimar Republic after World War I; Treaty of Versailles; Economic Crisis (1923) and Great Depression.
Hitler's Rise to Power: Nazi propaganda, speechcraft, Enabling Act of 1933, establishment of totalitarian dictatorship.
The Nazi Worldview: Racial hierarchy, Nordic Aryans, Anti-Semitism, Lebensraum (living space).
Youth in Nazi Germany: Jungvolk, Hitler Youth; Motherhood cult.
The Holocaust: Ghettos, gas chambers, Nuremberg trials.
learning_outcomes: Understand the humiliating impact of the Treaty of Versailles on Germany.
Explain the political and economic conditions that enabled Hitler's fascist dictatorship.
Sensitize students against racism, discrimination, and genocide.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain why the Weimar Republic was politically fragile in Germany.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: జర్మనీలో వీమర్ రిపబ్లిక్ రాజకీయంగా ఎందుకు బలహీనంగా ఉండిందో వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What was the Holocaust? Why is it considered one of the darkest chapters in human history?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: హోలోకాస్ట్ (మారణహోమం) అంటే ఏమిటి? మానవ చరిత్రలో ఇది అత్యంత చీకటి అధ్యాయంగా ఎందుకు పరిగణించబడుతుంది?

core_themes: Deforestation under British Rule: Timber for Royal Navy, railway sleepers, commercial crops (tea, coffee, rubber).
Scientific Forestry: Dietrich Brandis, Indian Forest Act of 1865 and 1878 amendments (Reserved, Protected, Village forests).
Impact on forest dwellers: Shifting cultivation banned, hunting criminalized, forced labour.
Rebellion in the Forest: Bastar rebellion (1910) led by Gunda Dhur; Dutch forest laws in Java (Blandongdiensten system) and Saminist movement.
learning_outcomes: Understand the commercial and imperial reasons for British deforestation in India.
Examine the loss of tribal livelihoods and autonomy under colonial forest laws.
Compare forest resistance in Bastar (India) with Java (Indonesia).

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain why the British introduced 'Scientific Forestry' in India. What were its consequences for forest communities?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: బ్రిటిష్ వారు భారతదేశంలో 'శాస్త్రీయ అటవీ విధానాన్ని' ఎందుకు ప్రవేశపెట్టారు? అటవీ సమాజాలపై దాని పరిణామాలు ఏమిటి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: How did the 1910 Bastar Rebellion reflect the grievances of indigenous tribal communities?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: 1910 బస్తర్ తిరుగుబాటు స్థానిక ఆదివాసీ తెగల సమస్యలను ఎలా ప్రతిబింబించింది?

core_themes: Pastoral Nomads in India: Gujjar Bakarwals (Jammu & Kashmir), Gaddis (Himachal Pradesh), Dhangars (Maharashtra), Raikas (Rajasthan).
Colonial Rule and Pastoral Life: Waste Land Rules, Forest Acts, Criminal Tribes Act of 1871, Grazing tax.
Pastoralism in Africa: Maasai community of East Africa, loss of grazing lands, creation of game reserves (Serengeti, Maasai Mara).
learning_outcomes: Understand pastoral nomadic life as an ecologically sustainable adaptation to arid and mountain environments.
Examine how colonial borders, grazing taxes, and wildlife reserves destroyed traditional pastoral economies.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain how the seasonal movement of the Gujjar Bakarwals is adapted to the mountain environment.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: గుజ్జర్ బకర్వాల్స్ పశువుల కాపరుల కాలానుగుణ వలసలు పర్వత పర్యావరణానికి ఎలా అనుగుణంగా ఉంటాయో వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why did the colonial state consider pastoralists as unproductive and view mobile communities with suspicion?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: వలస పాలకులు పశుపోషకులను నిరుపయోగమైన వారిగా ఎందుకు భావించారు మరియు సంచార జాతులను అనుమానంతో ఎందుకు చూశారు?

core_themes: Location: Entirely in Northern Hemisphere; Latitudes 8°4'N to 37°6'N, Longitudes 68°7'E to 97°25'E.
Tropic of Cancer (23°30'N) divides India into almost two equal halves.
Size: Total area 3.28 million sq km (2.4% of total world area); 7th largest country; Land boundary 15,200 km; Coastline 7,516.6 km.
Standard Meridian of India (82°30'E passing through Mirzapur in UP); IST is GMT + 5:30.
India and the World: Strategic central location at head of Indian Ocean; Neighbours (Pakistan, Afghanistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Maldives).
learning_outcomes: Locate India's latitudinal and longitudinal extent on the world globe.
Understand why 82°30'E longitude was selected as the Standard Meridian of India.
Identify India's strategic maritime and land neighbours.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: The sun rises two hours earlier in Arunachal Pradesh as compared to Gujarat in the west, but the watches show the same time. How does this happen?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: గుజరాత్‌తో పోలిస్తే అరుణాచల్ ప్రదేశ్‌లో సూర్యుడు రెండు గంటల ముందే ఉదయిస్తాడు, కానీ గడియారాలు ఒకే సమయాన్ని చూపుతాయి. ఇది ఎలా సాధ్యం?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, identify and locate: (a) Tropic of Cancer, (b) Standard Meridian of India, (c) Southernmost tip of Indian mainland.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ అవుట్‌లైన్ మ్యాప్‌లో గుర్తించండి: (a) కర్కట రేఖ, (b) ప్రామాణిక రేఖాంశం (82°30' తూర్పు), (c) భారతదేశ ప్రధాన భూభాగ దక్షిణ అగ్రం (కన్యాకుమారి).

core_themes: Theory of Plate Tectonics: Convergent, Divergent, Transform boundaries; Gondwanaland breakup.
The Himalayan Mountains: Himadri (Greater Himalayas), Himachal (Lesser Himalayas), Shiwaliks (Outer Himalayas).
The Northern Plains: Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar, Khadar; Alluvial deposits of Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra.
The Peninsular Plateau: Central Highlands, Deccan Plateau, Western Ghats (Anamudi 2695 m), Eastern Ghats (Mahendragiri 1501 m).
The Indian Desert (Thar), The Coastal Plains (Konkan, Kannad, Malabar, Coromandel, Northern Circars), and The Islands (Lakshadweep, Andaman and Nicobar).
learning_outcomes: Understand tectonic plate movements creating Himalayas and Indo-Gangetic plains.
Compare the physical features of Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats.
Classify Northern Plains based on relief features.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Distinguish between Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: పశ్చిమ కనుమలు మరియు తూర్పు కనుమల మధ్య గల భేదాలను రాయండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Contrast the relief of the Himalayan region with that of the Peninsular plateau.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: హిమాలయ ప్రాంత భౌగోళిక స్వరూపాలను ద్వీపకల్ప పీఠభూమి స్వరూపాలతో పోల్చి భేదాలను రాయండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, locate and label: Kanchenjunga peak, Chota Nagpur plateau, and Malabar Coast.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ అవుట్‌లైన్ మ్యాప్‌లో కాంచన్‌జంగా శిఖరం, చోటానాగ్‌పూర్ పీఠభూమి, మలబార్ తీరాలను గుర్తించండి.

core_themes: Drainage basins, water divides, and drainage patterns (Dendritic, Trellis, Rectangular, Radial).
Himalayan Rivers: The Indus River System, The Ganga River System, The Brahmaputra River System (perennial, antecedent).
Peninsular Rivers: Narmada and Tapi (rift valleys, flowing into Arabian Sea), Godavari (Dakshin Ganga), Mahanadi, Krishna, Kaveri (flowing into Bay of Bengal).
Lakes of India: Fresh water lakes (Wular, Dal, Nainital, Loktak) and Salt water lakes (Sambhar, Chilika, Pulicat).
Role of rivers in the economy and National River Conservation Plan (NRCP).
learning_outcomes: Distinguish between Himalayan and Peninsular river systems.
Explain the economic importance of freshwater lakes and rivers in agriculture and power generation.
Identify causes of river pollution and measures for river cleaning.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Compare the east-flowing and west-flowing rivers of the Peninsular plateau.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ద్వీపకల్ప పీఠభూమిలోని తూర్పుగా ప్రవహించే నదులు మరియు పశ్చిమంగా ప్రవహించే నదులను పోల్చండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, trace the course of the River Godavari and River Narmada, and mark Chilika Lake.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ పటంలో గోదావరి, నర్మదా నదుల ప్రవాహ మార్గాలను మరియు చిల్కా సరస్సును గుర్తించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why are rivers considered the lifelines of human civilization? Mention two steps to prevent river pollution.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: నదులను మానవ నాగరికతకు జీవనాధారాలుగా ఎందుకు పరిగణిస్తారు? నదీ కాలుష్యాన్ని నివారించే రెండు మార్గాలను తెలపండి.

core_themes: Difference between weather and climate.
Climatic controls: Latitude, Altitude, Pressure and wind systems, Distance from the sea (Continentality), Ocean currents, Relief.
Mechanism of the Indian Monsoon: ITCZ (Inter Tropical Convergence Zone), El Nino, Southern Oscillation (ENSO), Jet Streams.
Seasons of India: Cold weather season (Winter), Hot weather season (Summer), Advancing Monsoon (South-West Monsoon), Retreating Monsoon (North-East Monsoon / Cyclones).
Distribution of rainfall and Monsoon as a unifying bond.
learning_outcomes: Explain the factors influencing the climate of India.
Describe the mechanism of onset and withdrawal of the monsoon.
Analyze the distribution of rainfall across western coast vs interior Deccan.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What are the six major climatic controls of any place?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఏదైనా ప్రాంతం యొక్క శీతోష్ణస్థితిని నియంత్రించే ఆరు ప్రధాన కారకాలు ఏవి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why does the Coromandel Coast receive winter rainfall?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: కోరమాండల్ తీరానికి శీతాకాలంలో వర్షపాతం ఎందుకు లభిస్తుంది?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, locate Mawsynram (highest rainfall in the world) and regions receiving less than 20 cm rainfall.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ పటంలో ప్రపంచంలోనే అత్యధిక వర్షపాతం నమోదయ్యే మాసిన్‌రామ్ మరియు 20 సెం.మీ. కంటే తక్కువ వర్షపాతం పొందే ప్రాంతాలను గుర్తించండి.

core_themes: Factors affecting diversity of flora and fauna: Relief (Land, Soil) and Climate (Temperature, Photoperiod, Precipitation).
Types of Vegetation: Tropical Evergreen Forests, Tropical Deciduous Forests (Monsoon forests), Tropical Thorn Forests and Scrubs, Montane Forests, Mangrove Forests (Sundarbans).
Wildlife diversity in India; Endemic and endangered species.
Conservation of Forests and Wildlife: National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries, Biosphere Reserves (18 in India, e.g. Nilgiri, Sunderbans).
learning_outcomes: Identify ecological conditions required for various natural vegetation types in India.
Understand the importance of Sundarbans mangroves and biodiversity conservation.
Appreciate wildlife protection laws (Wildlife Protection Act 1972).

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Distinguish between Tropical Evergreen Forests and Tropical Deciduous Forests.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఉష్ణమండల సతతహరిత అరణ్యాలు మరియు ఉష్ణమండల ఆకురాల్చే అడవుల మధ్య గల భేదాలను వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: On an outline map of India, mark Kaziranga National Park, Gir Forest, and Sundarbans Biosphere Reserve.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశ పటంలో కాజిరంగా జాతీయ ఉద్యానవనం, గిర్ అభయారణ్యం, మరియు సుందర్‌బన్స్ బయోస్పియర్ రిజర్వ్‌లను గుర్తించండి.

core_themes: Population Size and Distribution: Census of India, population density (people per sq km).
Population Growth and Processes of Population Change: Birth rate, Death rate, Migration (Internal and International).
Age Composition: Children (below 15), Working age (15-59), Aged (60+); Dependency ratio.
Sex Ratio: Number of females per 1000 males; Literacy rate.
Occupational Structure: Primary, Secondary, Tertiary sectors; National Population Policy (NPP 2000).
learning_outcomes: Explain the components of population change: fertility, mortality, and migration.
Interpret population pyramids and age sex composition.
Understand key objectives of National Population Policy 2000.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What are the three main components of population change? Explain how each influences population growth.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: జనాభా మార్పుకు గల మూడు ప్రధాన కారకాలు ఏవి? ప్రతి ఒక్కటి జనాభా పెరుగుదలను ఎలా ప్రభావితం చేస్తుందో వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What is meant by Sex Ratio? Why is a favorable sex ratio considered an indicator of women empowerment?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: స్త్రీ-పురుష నిష్పత్తి (సెక్స్ రేషియో) అనగా ఏమిటి? అనుకూలమైన స్త్రీ-పురుష నిష్పత్తి మహిళా సాధికారతకు సూచికగా ఎందుకు పరిగణించబడుతుంది?

core_themes: Simple Definition: Democracy is a form of government in which rulers are elected by the people.

Features of Democracy: Major decisions by elected leaders (Pakistan under Musharraf case); Free and fair electoral competition (China and Mexico cases); One person, one vote, one value (Fiji, Saudi Arabia, Estonia cases); Rule of law and respect for rights (Zimbabwe under Mugabe case).
Arguments against Democracy: Instability, delays, political competition, corruption.
Arguments for Democracy: Accountable government, improves decision quality, accommodates diversity, enhances dignity of citizens.
learning_outcomes: Distinguish between genuine democracy and facade democratic systems.
Critically evaluate arguments for and against democracy.
Appreciate the democratic principles of equality, accountability, and rule of law.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain the four core features of a democratic government.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ప్రజాస్వామ్య ప్రభుత్వానికి గల నాలుగు ముఖ్యమైన లక్షణాలను వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: 'Democracy is better than any other form of government in responding to the needs of the people.' Justify this statement with examples.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: 'ప్రజల అవసరాలకు స్పందించడంలో ప్రజాస్వామ్యం ఇతర ప్రభుత్వ రూపాల కంటే మెరుగైనది.' ఉదాహరణలతో ఈ ప్రకటనను సమర్థించండి.

core_themes: Democratic Constitution in South Africa: Apartheid struggle, Nelson Mandela, transition to non-racial democracy in 1994.
Why do we need a Constitution? Establishes trust, specifies decision-making authority, limits government power, expresses aspirations.
Making of the Indian Constitution: Constituent Assembly, Motilal Nehru draft (1928), Karachi session (1931), Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.
Guiding Values of the Indian Constitution: Preamble: Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic, Justice, Liberty, Equality, Fraternity.
learning_outcomes: Understand the struggle against apartheid and the making of South African constitution.
Analyze the historical consensus and debates within India's Constituent Assembly.
Examine the core constitutional values enshrined in the Preamble.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What were the challenges faced by the makers of the Indian Constitution during its drafting?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారత రాజ్యాంగ రూపకల్పన సమయంలో రాజ్యాంగ నిర్మాతలు ఎదుర్కొన్న ప్రధాన సవాళ్లు ఏమిటి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Read the Preamble to the Constitution of India. Explain the significance of the terms 'Secular' and 'Republic'.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారత రాజ్యాంగ ప్రవేశికను చదివి, అందులోని 'లౌకిక' మరియు 'గణతంత్ర' పదాల అంతరార్థాన్ని వివరించండి.

core_themes: Why Elections? Mechanism for citizens to choose representatives and policy makers.
What makes an election democratic? Universal adult suffrage, genuine choices, regular intervals, free and fair process.
Electoral system in India: Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha constituencies, Reserved constituencies for SC and ST.
Voters' list (Electoral Roll), Nomination of candidates, Election campaign, Model Code of Conduct, Polling and counting.
Independent Election Commission of India (ECI): Powers, autonomous constitutional status, acceptance of election outcomes.
learning_outcomes: Understand how periodic elections ensure representative democratic accountability.
Evaluate the powers and constitutional independence of the Election Commission of India.
Explain provisions ensuring free, fair, and inclusive elections.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What powers make the Election Commission of India independent and powerful?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారత ఎన్నికల సంఘానికి గల ఏ అధికారాలు దానిని స్వతంత్రమైన మరియు శక్తివంతమైన సంస్థగా నిలబెడుతున్నాయి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What is the Model Code of Conduct for election campaigns? Mention any three prohibitions under it.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఎన్నికల ప్రవర్తనా నియమావళి (మోడల్ కోడ్ ఆఫ్ కండక్ట్) అంటే ఏమిటి? దాని కింద విధించిన ఏవైనా మూడు నిబంధనలను పేర్కొనండి.

core_themes: How a Major Policy Decision is Taken: Office Memorandum example, Mandal Commission report.
Parliament: Need for political institutions, two Houses (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha), powers comparison.
Political Executive: Difference between Political Executive (Ministers) and Permanent Executive (Civil Servants).
Prime Minister and Council of Ministers: Cabinet, powers of Prime Minister; President of India (Head of State).
Judiciary: Supreme Court of India, High Courts, Judicial Review, Public Interest Litigation (PIL), Independence of Judiciary.
learning_outcomes: Analyze the division of powers between Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary.
Compare the legislative and financial powers of Lok Sabha versus Rajya Sabha.
Understand the independence of judiciary and judicial review.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why does the Lok Sabha exercise supreme power over the Rajya Sabha in matters of money bills?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ధన బిల్లుల విషయంలో రాజ్యసభ కంటే లోక్‌సభకు అత్యున్నత అధికారాలు ఎందుకు ఉన్నాయి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Distinguish between the Political Executive and the Permanent Executive.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: రాజకీయ కార్యనిర్వాహక వర్గం మరియు శాశ్వత కార్యనిర్వాహక వర్గం (సివిల్ సర్వీసెస్) మధ్య గల భేదాలను వివరించండి.

core_themes: Life without rights: Prison in Guantanamo Bay (US), Citizens' rights in Saudi Arabia, Ethnic massacre in Kosovo.
Rights in a Democracy: Definition of rights as reasonable claims of persons recognized by society and sanctioned by law.

Fundamental Rights in the Indian Constitution: Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, Right to Constitutional Remedies (Article 32).
Expanding scope of rights: RTI, Right to Education, Human Rights Commission.
learning_outcomes: Appreciate the vital role of constitutional fundamental rights in protecting individual liberty.
Examine Article 32 as the 'Heart and Soul of the Constitution' (Ambedkar).
Understand the evolving landscape of socioeconomic human rights.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Why is the Right to Constitutional Remedies considered the heart and soul of our Constitution?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: రాజ్యాంగ పరిహార హక్కును మన రాజ్యాంగానికి గుండెకాయ మరియు ఆత్మగా ఎందుకు భావిస్తారు?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain how the Right to Equality protects citizens against discrimination in India.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశంలో పౌరులను వివక్ష నుండి సమానత్వపు హక్కు ఏ విధంగా కాపాడుతుందో వివరించండి.

core_themes: Overview of production: Organization of production (Land, Labour, Physical Capital, Human Capital).
Farming in Palampur: Land is fixed; Multiple cropping, Green Revolution with HYV seeds, chemical fertilizers, irrigation tube-wells.
Impact of Green Revolution on soil fertility and groundwater depletion.
Land distribution among farmers: Small vs medium and large farmers.
Non-farm activities in Palampur: Dairy farming, small-scale manufacturing, shopkeeping, transport services.
learning_outcomes: Understand the four essential factors of production: Land, Labour, Capital, and Enterprise.
Examine the benefits and ecological drawbacks of Green Revolution agricultural modernization.
Identify non-farm rural livelihood opportunities.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain the four requirements for the production of goods and services.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: వస్తువులు మరియు సేవల ఉత్పత్తికి అవసరమైన నాలుగు ప్రధాన కారకాలను వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What are the environmental hazards associated with excessive use of chemical fertilizers in Green Revolution farming?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: హరిత విప్లవ వ్యవసాయంలో రసాయన ఎరువుల మితిమీరిన వినియోగం వల్ల కలిగే పర్యావరణ ముప్పులు ఏమిటి?

core_themes: Overview: Human capital formation through investment in education, training, and healthcare.
Economic Activities by Men and Women: Primary, Secondary, and Tertiary sectors; Market and non-market activities.
Quality of Population: Education (literacy rates, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan), Health (life expectancy, infant mortality rate).
Unemployment: Disguised unemployment, Seasonal unemployment in rural areas, Educated unemployment in urban areas.
Consequences of unemployment: Wastage of manpower, economic overload, social unrest.
learning_outcomes: Understand how human capital increases productivity and national income.
Differentiate between seasonal and disguised unemployment.
Examine public investment in education and public healthcare systems.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What is the difference between economic activities and non-economic activities?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ఆర్థిక కార్యకలాపాలు మరియు ఆర్థికేతర కార్యకలాపాల మధ్య గల వ్యత్యాసం ఏమిటి?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What is disguised unemployment? Give an agricultural example.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: ప్రచ్ఛన్న నిరుద్యోగం అనగా ఏమిటి? వ్యవసాయ రంగం నుండి ఒక ఉదాహరణ ఇవ్వండి.

core_themes: Dimensions of poverty: Hunger, lack of shelter, safe drinking water, healthcare, sanitation, job insecurity.
Poverty as seen by social scientists: Social exclusion, vulnerability.
Poverty Line concept: Minimum subsistence level, calorie norms (2400 rural, 2100 urban), monetary value.
Poverty estimates in India; Vulnerable groups (SC, ST, landless agricultural labourers).
Inter-state disparities in poverty (high in Bihar, Odisha; low in Kerala, Punjab).
Anti-Poverty Measures: Promotion of economic growth; Targeted anti-poverty programmes: MGNREGA 2005, PMRY, PMGY, AAY.
learning_outcomes: Understand the multidimensional nature of poverty and poverty line estimation.
Analyze inter-state and social group disparities in poverty incidence.
Evaluate government welfare and employment generation schemes (MGNREGA).

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: How is the poverty line estimated in India? Explain the calorie and monetary criteria.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశంలో పేదరిక రేఖను ఎలా అంచనా వేస్తారు? కేలరీల వినియోగం మరియు ఆదాయ ప్రమాణాలను వివరించండి.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Discuss the major features of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) 2005.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: మహాత్మా గాంధీ జాతీయ గ్రామీణ ఉపాధి హామీ చట్టం (MGNREGA) 2005 యొక్క ముఖ్య లక్షణాలను చర్చించండి.

core_themes: What is Food Security? Availability, Accessibility, and Affordability of food to all citizens.
Why Food Security? Famine of Bengal (1943), disaster mitigation, food insecurity during natural calamities.
Who are Food-Insecure? Landless agricultural labourers, traditional artisans, urban casual workers, vulnerable castes.
Food Security System in India: Buffer Stock (FCI procurement at Minimum Support Price - MSP) and Public Distribution System (PDS - Fair Price Shops).
Role of Cooperatives in Food Security: Amul (Gujarat), Mother Dairy (Delhi), Academy of Development Science (Grain banks in Maharashtra).
learning_outcomes: Understand the triple pillars of food security: Availability, Accessibility, Affordability.
Explain the functioning of Buffer Stock and the Public Distribution System (PDS).
Appreciate the vital role of agricultural and consumer cooperatives in ensuring food security.

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: What is Buffer Stock? Why is it created by the government?
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: బఫర్ స్టాక్ (నిల్వ ఆహార ధాన్యాలు) అనగా ఏమిటి? ప్రభుత్వం దీనిని ఎందుకు నిర్వహిస్తుంది?

chapter_end_exercises.question_text_en: Explain the role of the Public Distribution System (PDS) in ensuring food security in India.
chapter_end_exercises.question_text_te: భారతదేశంలో ఆహార భద్రతను కల్పించడంలో ప్రజా పంపిణీ వ్యవస్థ (PDS) పోషిస్తున్న పాత్రను వివరించండి.
